entities.name: PMID:25445398
observations: In mice fed a saturated-fat/high-cholesterol/high-fructose diet, deletion of the murine TRAIL receptor reduced adiposity, insulin resistance, steatohepatitis, hepatocyte apoptosis, hepatic triglycerides, and inflammatory macrophage accumulation/activation in liver and adipose tissue.
Receptor-null bone-marrow macrophages showed reduced chemotaxis and NF-kB activation after palmitate or LPS stimulation.

entities.name: PMID:29124251
observations: Trail ligand deletion in an FFC-diet model reduced liver injury and inflammation but did not improve adipose inflammation and worsened insulin resistance, distinguishing ligand deletion from receptor deletion.

entities.name: Murine TRAIL receptor
observations: The single murine TRAIL receptor is commonly termed TRAIL-R/DR5 and is generally mapped to Tnfrsf10b; the reported receptor-null phenotype is not evidence for separate knockout of human TNFRSF10A and TNFRSF10B paralogs.

entities.name: TRAIL receptor deletion suppresses nutrient inflammation
observations: In the reported mouse FFC-diet model, murine TRAIL receptor deletion suppressed hepatic and adipose macrophage-associated inflammation and related metabolic injury.
This conclusion is specific to the single murine TRAIL-R/DR5 receptor model and should not be conflated with TRAIL-ligand deletion.
